title: Gamma ray burst may have been two supernovae in one | New Scientist
description: A group of astronomers proposes that a series of events in a distant galaxy formed both a black hole and a pulsar, but other experts say the conclusion is premature
author: Matt von Hippel

title: Exquisite 66-million-year-old bird feather preserved in dinosaur dropping | New Scientist
description: A dinosaur, possibly a young Tyrannosaurus rex, excreted a bird 66 million years ago, and one of its feathers is exquisitely preserved in the fossilised dropping
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Here is how to understand OpenAI’s major mathematical breakthrough | New Scientist
description: Since OpenAI announced its solution to one of the prestigious Millennium Prize Problems, mathematicians have been urgently trying to unpick what it means
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: The world’s biggest carbon sink may start emitting CO2 after net zero | New Scientist
description: If the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere declines, the Southern Ocean is likely to begin emitting more carbon than it absorbs, prolonging global warming
author: Alec Luhn

title: What's next for mathematics now that AI is upending the field? | New Scientist
description: Famous and challenging problems in mathematics are falling to AI at a rapid pace. Where does this leave mathematicians, and what will the field look like in coming years?
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: August was the joint hottest month on record | New Scientist
description: Global warming and a record El Niño have pushed Earth’s temperature more than 1.5°C above the pre-industrial average, and further heat is on the way
author: Alec Luhn
